subject.title: [Bug]: Unawaited persistGatewaySessionLifecycleEvent swallows write failures and drops session start markers

question: Should Gateway start lifecycle persistence become a blocking durability boundary for recoverable runs, or should OpenClaw keep the current best-effort log-only behavior?
rationale: The current path logs write failures, but making start markers durable could change hot-path latency, failure semantics, and restart-recovery ownership, so automation should not choose that policy silently.

options.title: Design A Bounded Durability Fix
options.body: Make start marker persistence or an equivalent recovery record part of the admitted-run lifecycle, with tests for rejected writes and restart/crash recovery.

options.title: Keep Log-Only Semantics
options.body: Accept that start marker loss is diagnosable but not recovered when storage rejects or the process exits before the write settles.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Restart Recovery
options.body: Track this under a broader restart-recovery redesign if maintainers want one recovery-state model for start, terminal, crash, and cross-boot cases.

recommendation.title: Design A Bounded Durability Fix
recommendation.body: Make start marker persistence or an equivalent recovery record part of the admitted-run lifecycle, with tests for rejected writes and restart/crash recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the current start logging behavior and has recent adjacent ownership across Gateway session lifecycle persistence cleanup.
